title: REAL passed to DOUBLE PRECISION parameter loses precision silently
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE COMPUTE_NORM(X, Y, NORM)
C     Caller-supplied X and Y are REAL*4 (single precision). The
C     callee declares NORM as DOUBLE PRECISION. F77 silently widens
C     each operand and stores the double result -- but the inputs
C     already lost precision before they got here. A modernised
C     version that types everything as 'double' will diverge by ~1e-7
      IMPLICIT NONE
      REAL              X, Y
      DOUBLE PRECISION  NORM
      DOUBLE PRECISION  DX, DY

C     Widening REAL -> DOUBLE here preserves the bits already lost.
      DX   = DBLE(X)
      DY   = DBLE(Y)
      NORM = SQRT(DX*DX + DY*DY)
      RETURN
      END
notes:
Mixed-precision Fortran calls are everywhere in numerical-library
legacy code (BLAS / LAPACK / MINPACK all have REAL and DOUBLE
variants of the same routine). Migrating to a language with one
'double' default silently changes the precision contract --
results will differ in the 7th decimal. The spec must capture
the call-site precision AND surface the tolerance/equality
question for the SME before the rewrite picks one.
